blocks.content: This topic goes past the Networking module's overview into the actual, ordered sequence of what happens when a Pod starts, including a detail almost everyone misses: kubelet creates a "sandbox" before the CNI plugin is even called.

When a new Pod needs networking, four things happen in strict order: kubelet creates a Pod sandbox, calls the CNI plugin's ADD operation, the plugin allocates an IP and sets up routing, and finally returns the result back to kubelet.

blocks.alt: A strict, four-step sequence, not one undifferentiated networking setup step

blocks.content: 2. The Sandbox: a Detail Worth Knowing
blocks.text: 2. The Sandbox: a Detail Worth Knowing

blocks.content: Before any real containers start, kubelet creates a Pod sandbox, in practice, a special, minimal pause container whose sole purpose is holding the Pod's network namespace steady, this is exactly what lets other containers in the same Pod share one consistent network identity, covered back in the What is a Pod topic.

blocks.alt: A special, minimal container, existing purely to hold the Pod's shared network identity steady

blocks.content: With the sandbox's network namespace established, kubelet calls the configured CNI plugin's ADD operation, handing it that exact network namespace to actually configure.

blocks.alt: The precise handoff, kubelet's sandbox namespace, given to the CNI plugin to configure

blocks.content: The CNI plugin allocates a real IP address for the Pod, and sets up the low-level networking, commonly a veth (virtual ethernet) pair connecting the Pod's namespace to the host, plus the routing needed to make the flat Pod-to-Pod network model covered in the Networking module actually work.

blocks.alt: The genuine, low-level networking work that makes the flat Pod network model actually real

blocks.content: Once the plugin returns its result, the Pod's networking is fully live, only at this point can the actual application containers, started afterward, meaningfully use the network at all.

blocks.alt: The exact moment a Pod's networking becomes real and usable

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: kubelet creates a Pod sandbox (the pause container) before calling the CNI plugin at all, this is exactly what holds a Pod's shared network identity steady.
The CNI plugin allocates an IP and sets up real routing (commonly a veth pair) in response to a CNI ADD call, only then is the Pod's networking actually live.
